_doc: Recurring-cost experiment. ONE policy with a buried, counterintuitive OVERRIDE that beats the headline rule. Every case hinges on the SAME shared fact (the override). The default rule cues ENTITLED (distance > 50 mi, stated prominently); the override quietly flips it to NOT_ENTITLED when the destination is a property the employee already owned. Fast prose reasoning anchors on the prominent distance and misses the buried override — and because each answer is a stateless call, that error RECURS on every case with no way to install a durable fix. The framework encodes the override as a rule ONCE; the engine then decides every case (present + held-out) deterministically at zero answer-time model calls.
policy:
Relocation Bonus Policy.
Section 1. An employee who relocates their primary residence more than 50 miles closer to their assigned work site is entitled to the relocation bonus.
Section 2. Override: The relocation bonus does not apply when the destination residence is a property the employee (or their spouse) already owned at the time the role was offered. This self-owned-destination exclusion applies regardless of distance.
question: Is the employee entitled to the relocation bonus? Answer ENTITLED or NOT_ENTITLED.
shared_fact: destination_already_owned (the Section 2 override) is dispositive in every override case and beats the Section 1 distance rule.

slots_schema.relocation_distance_miles: numeric — miles relocated closer to the work site
slots_schema.destination_already_owned: true/false — did the employee (or spouse) already own the destination residence when the role was offered
